A step that runs a program

Source: R/core-verify-command.R
hr_step_command.Rd

hr_step_command() builds a step that runs one program you name, such as Rscript on a test file, and reads its result as "passed" or "failed". Put it in a chain after the step that writes what it checks, so a benchmark can count how often a draft passes.

Usage

hr_step_command(
  name,
  argv,
  parse = c("exit", "testthat"),
  timeout = 60,
  held = FALSE,
  wd = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The step's name, one string.

argv

The command: a character vector whose first element is the program and the rest its arguments, or a function of (input, ctx) that returns one, such as a vector that names a file the step before it wrote.

parse

How the result is read: "exit" or "testthat".

timeout

Seconds the program may run before it is stopped, from 1 to 86400.

held

Whether the result is kept from the steps after this one and left for the scorer.

wd

The folder the program runs in, or NULL for the current one. The working directory is set back afterwards.

Value

A step (see hr_step()) of class c("hr_step_command", "hr_step", "function") with the settings parse, timeout and held, which hr_set() and hr_sweep() change by path, as "check.timeout". The result it records is a list of class hr_command_result: name, argv, status, exit (the exit code, or NA), seconds, degradation (NA unless timed out), counts (for "testthat": fail, warn, skip and pass, else NULL), and stdout and stderr, each cut to its last 64 KB.

Details

The command runs through base system2() with the user's own privileges. Each element of argv is one argument: they are quoted for the shell, never split on spaces, so a ; or a $ in an argument reaches the program as it is written. There is no default command, and a command is never taken from a model's reply or a skill's text: write argv yourself. Nothing isolates the program: it can read and write what you can. The child process inherits the session's environment variables, except OPENAI_API_KEY, which is unset for the call and put back after it; R options never reach it. A program stopped at its time limit is ended, but processes it started in the background (or that ignore the signal) can keep running, on any platform; on Windows, any process it started can.

The result is read by parse:

"exit"

"passed" when the program exits with 0, else "failed".

"testthat"

The last [ FAIL n | WARN n | SKIP n | PASS n ] line the program printed: "failed" when FAIL is above 0, "passed" when it is 0 and the program exits with 0. With no such line, or a summary of no failures and a non-zero exit, the status is "error". The exit code alone is not read, since testthat::test_file() exits with 0 when a test fails unless it is given stop_on_failure = TRUE. Use a reporter that prints the summary line, such as the default, "progress" or "check": under "summary" no such line is printed and the status is "error". stop_on_failure = TRUE makes the exit code agree with the result.

A program stopped at timeout seconds is "timeout", with the degradation "command_timeout", and a program that cannot be found is "error". No warning from system2() reaches the caller.

With held = FALSE the step returns its input, a list, with the result in $check, so the next step can read it (a revise step, say). With held = TRUE the next step must not see it: the step returns its input unchanged, records the status as the signal "command.<step>" (see hr_signal()), and attaches the result to the output as attr(output, "hr_held"), a list named by step, which a scorer from hr_scorer() reads. A held step must come last: hr_chain() refuses a step that is not held after one that is, with class hr_held_not_last.

In a benchmark the step notes the run in the trace as a local step, "step.command", with hashes of argv and of the output, never the output itself. It sends no request, so it costs nothing.

hr_step(), hr_chain(), hr_scorer()

Examples

rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
check <- hr_step_command("check", c(rscript, "-e", "quit(status = 0)"))
check(list(draft = "x"), list())$check$status
#> [1] "passed"

# The command can depend on the step's input.
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines("stopifnot(1 + 1 == 2)", f)
run_file <- hr_step_command("run", function(input, ctx) c(rscript, input$file))
run_file(list(file = f), list())$check$status
#> [1] "passed"

# Held back from later steps, for the scorer.
ref <- hr_reference(list(q1 = "f"), labels = "passed", cluster = "a", split = "test")
chain <- hr_chain(
  draft = hr_step("draft", function(input, ctx) list(item = input)),
  check = hr_step_command("check", c(rscript, "-e", "quit(status = 1)"),
                          held = TRUE),
  name = "held")
passes <- hr_scorer(function(item, output, label) {
  s <- attr(output, "hr_held")$check$status
  list(correct = identical(s, label), outcome = s, failure_kind = NA)
}, name = "passes")
bench <- hr_benchmark(chain, ref, runs = 5, client = NULL, scorer = passes)
table(bench$outcome)
#> 
#> failed 
#>      5 
unlink(f)
